_comment: Research sweep definition for SyncroEffects. Run with: python run_sweep.py. Each block defines a sensitivity study — one parameter varies while all others are held constant. run_sweep.py computes the cartesian product of ev × pv × hp × seasons × scenarios per block and deduplicates across blocks. All sensitivity blocks (2–4, 7–9) use the same six strategies for comparability.

_scenarios.baseline: No EVs/HPs, PV sgens only — pure grid reference
_scenarios.fixed_times: All EVs charge simultaneously at 18:00 — worst-case synchronisation
_scenarios.fixed_random: Each EV has its own randomised start time — uncoordinated but spread
_scenarios.decentral: Decentralised HEMS, spot price only — self-interested, no grid awareness
_scenarios.decentral_m3: Decentralised HEMS, §14a Modul-3 grid fee added to spot price (Q1/Q4 only)
_scenarios.central_cost: Centralised LP, minimise total energy cost with transformer limit
_scenarios.central_peak: Centralised LP, minimise peak transformer load
_scenarios.central_flat: Centralised LP, minimise load variance (flatten load profile)

Block1_core._comment: Core synchronisation comparison: all six strategies, all seasons, reference penetration EV=PV=HP=30%.

Block2_ev_sweep._comment: EV penetration sensitivity (PV=HP=0%). All six strategies. Isolates the pure EV synchronisation effect. Winter = worst case (no solar relief). Compare against Block7 (PV+HP=30%) to see the device-interaction effect.

Block3_pv_sweep._comment: PV penetration sensitivity (EV=30%, HP=0%). All six strategies. Summer vs winter contrast isolates seasonal PV yield differences. Compare against Block8 (HP=30%) to see the HP interaction with PV.

Block4_hp_sweep._comment: HP penetration sensitivity (EV=30%, PV=0%). All six strategies. Winter = highest heating demand; PV=0% so the HP effect is not masked by solar. Compare against Block9 (PV=30%) to see the PV interaction with HP.

Block5_module3._comment: §14a EnWG Modul-3 regulatory sensitivity. Compares decentralised HEMS with and without the time-variable grid fee. The fee applies only in Q1 (Jan–Mar) and Q4 (Oct–Dec) per the Norderstedt tariff structure; winter (week 3) falls in Q1, autumn (week 41) falls in Q4. Spring/summer are excluded (Q2/Q3, fee = 0). PV=HP=0% to isolate the EV price-shifting effect.

Block7_ev_sweep_combined._comment: EV penetration sweep with PV and HP held fixed at 30%. All six strategies. Compare against Block2 (PV=HP=0%) to quantify the HP compounding effect and how PV cushions EV-driven overloads. Winter = worst case.

Block8_pv_sweep_combined._comment: PV penetration sweep with EV and HP held fixed at 30%. All six strategies. Summer vs winter contrast (high vs low PV yield). Compare against Block3 (HP=0%) to isolate the HP interaction with PV relief.

Block9_hp_sweep_combined._comment: HP penetration sweep with EV and PV held fixed at 30%. All six strategies. Compare against Block4 (PV=0%) to isolate the PV interaction with HP synchronisation.

Block6_module3_combined._comment: §14a Modul-3 with combined EV+PV+HP scenario (EV=PV=HP=30%). Needed for Fig. 1 strategy comparison at reference penetration. Fee applies in Q1 (winter) and Q4 (autumn).

Block_module3_hp_sweep._comment: §14a Modul-3 HP penetration sensitivity (EV=PV=0%). Pure HP scenario — no EVs — to show whether the fee provides relief when synchronisation is HP-driven. Winter (Q1) and autumn (Q4) only (fee-active seasons).
